title: Legal Invoices

communications.subject: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act Request: Legal Invoices
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of all legal services invoices and related billing records paid, received, or incurred by Thomaston Public Schools from July 1, 2025, through November 19, 2026.

This request includes all legal services provided to or on behalf of Thomaston Public Schools, the Thomaston Board of Education, the superintendent's office, district administration, individual schools, and any other department, office, employee, or representative acting in an official capacity.

This request is intended to encompass all legal services, regardless of their nature, purpose, subject matter, funding source, or the attorney or law firm providing the services. This includes, but is not limited to, general counsel, personnel and employment matters, labor relations, collective bargaining, grievances, litigation, investigations, contracts, special education, regulatory compliance, governance, and any other legal matters. These examples are illustrative and do not limit the scope of this request.

I specifically request complete, itemized invoices and billing statements, including, to the extent maintained, dates of service, descriptions of services performed, attorney or staff names, hours billed, hourly rates, expenses, and amounts charged. This request includes invoices that remain unpaid, as well as those already paid, and invoices paid through insurance, other governmental entities, or alternative funding arrangements, to the extent such records are maintained by the district.

I recognize that certain information may be protected by attorney-client privilege or another applicable exemption under Connecticut law. I am not requesting disclosure of privileged communications or legally exempt information. Where specific portions of an invoice are exempt, I request that only those portions be redacted and that all remaining nonexempt information be provided. Please do not withhold entire invoices solely because they contain some exempt information.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Sam Bellford

title: Sheriff's Emails with Federal Immigration Enforcement November 2026 (Suffolk County Sheriff's Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Emails with Federal Immigration Enforcement November 2026 (Suffolk County Sheriff's Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:
1. Visitor logs, sign-in sheets, gate, sallyport or vehicle entry logs, and records of custody transfers to a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” ICE employees accessing Sheriff’s department facilities, from September 4, 2026 through November 20, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to November 20, 2026).

2. From September 4, 2026 through November 20, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to November 20, 2026) all emails and any attachments between a Sheriff’s Department employee and a federal immigration authority. Email searches of “@ice.dhs.gov” can be a good place to begin to identify responsive records. 

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, county, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

On November 13, 2026, EPA Region 7 issued an emergency RCRA permit authorizing the intentional detonation of 9,500 pounds of degraded lead near the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. On November 19, Gov. Kim Reynolds’s spokesperson, Mason Mauro, told the Des Moines Register that the governor’s office only became aware of the planned detonation on November 16, when the Army issued a public advisory. A plume from the detonation could reach parts of Illinois.

I request all communications between the Illinois DPH, the federal EPA, and/or the Army between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

I also request all communications between DPH, the governor’s office, and/or any state agencies between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

I also request all communications between DPH and county and city authorities between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

Please include the following records:

- All external correspondence, including emails, text messages, letters, memoranda, and attachments
- All records of meetings, including calendar invites, video and/or audio recordings, transcripts, meeting agendas, presentations, and follow-up materials

I request expedited processing on the grounds that there is an urgency to inform the public about the timeline of this planned explosion and communication between federal and state agencies. The records requested have far-reaching implications for public health. Delayed disclosure of these records would compromise the public’s timely understanding of critical government functioning. As a journalist actively reporting on public health and environmental management, disseminating information about it to the public through articles for WIRED—which publishes stories based on documents received under the FOIA outside its paywall as a matter of policy—I have a compelling need for expedited access to this information.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Molly Taft
